async/collect#

Structured collection of futures.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let pending is @Future<int> = [
    Worker(id: 1).run(),
    Worker(id: 2).run(),
    Worker(id: 3).run(),
];
let collected is AllFutures<int> = AllFutures(origins: pending);
let values is Sequencing<int> = await collected.results();

Description#

Structured collection of futures.

AllFutures<T> starts every supplied future and publishes results in input order only after every future succeeds. The input may be any Sequencing object; it is read when results() starts, not during construction.

The returned sequence preserves input order rather than completion order. An empty input completes immediately with an empty sequence.

If one future fails, unfinished siblings are cancelled and their cleanup is awaited. The observed failure remains primary; the other failures follow as secondary diagnostics in input order, each failure once. A sibling whose own await had already completed when the cancellation came runs on to its next await, where the cancellation reaches it; if it fails before that, its failure is one of the secondaries. Cancelling results() applies the same structured cleanup rule. Repeated calls return the same future and never restart the inputs.

Raced<T> returns the value of the first settled input. A failing first settlement remains a failure; the race does not wait for a later success. Every loser is cancelled and fully cleaned before the result settles:

let race is Raced<Response> = Raced(origins: requests);
let response = await race.winner();

FirstSuccessful<T> instead ignores failed attempts while success is still possible. If all inputs fail, the first failure in completion order remains primary and later failures become ordered secondary diagnostics:

let attempts is FirstSuccessful<Response> = FirstSuccessful(
    origins: requests,
);
let response = await attempts.outcome();

Neither selector accepts an empty input; both throw NoFutures. A successful winner is not published when cancelling a loser exposes a cleanup failure.

FutureCompletions<T> exposes settlement order without turning a suspending operation into a synchronous cursor. completion() returns the original, already-settled Future<T> rather than extracting its value or failure:

let stream is FutureCompletions<Response> = FutureCompletions(
    origins: requests,
);

loop {
    last if stream.remaining_count() == 0;
    let completed = await stream.completion();
    try {
        let response = await completed;
        responses.write(response);
    }
    catch error is RequestFailed {
        failures.write(error);
    }
}

Every input position is returned once, including duplicate future identities. Concurrent completion requests and simultaneous settlements are paired FIFO; already-settled inputs are ordered by their input positions. Calling completion() after exhaustion throws NoFutures. Cancelling a pending completion request cancels the stream's unfinished inputs and waits for their cleanup; that request, and every request after it, fails with the cancellation (cleanup failures attached), not NoFutures.
